items.title: Spec-Driven Development: Building AI Aligned Software Through Living Specifications
items.summary: Artificial Intelligence is fundamentally transforming software development. As AI agents become increasingly capable of generating code, implementing features, and executing complex development tasks, the central challenge shifts from writing code to defining intent, controlling execution, verifying results, and preserving knowledge.This presentation, delivered by Haim Michael at All Day AI 2026 on October 22, 2026, explores Spec-Driven Development (SDD) as an approach to building reliable, maintainable, and AI-aligned software systems.The presentation begins by tracing the evolution beyond traditional code-first development and the limits of relying solely on vibe coding. Although vibe coding provides significant advantages for rapid experimentation and prototyping, professional software engineering requires reliability, traceability, and long-term maintainability.A key limitation is the lack of durable institutional memory. When architectural decisions and requirements exist primarily within conversations with AI assistants, maintaining and evolving complex systems becomes increasingly challenging.Spec-Driven Development addresses this challenge by introducing specifications as a shared foundation for humans and AI agents. Living specifications capture requirements, constraints, architectural decisions, and acceptance criteria, helping teams coordinate development while staying aligned with human intent.The presentation explores how to implement this approach using Kiro IDE, an agentic development environment designed to support structured, specification-driven workflows.Topics covered include:Spec-Driven Development fundamentals: Understanding the role of living specifications in AI-assisted software engineering.SDD versus vibe coding: Examining the differences between exploratory coding and structured professional development.Kiro IDE: Exploring an agentic development environment and its specification-driven capabilities.Steering documents: Providing AI agents with project context, architectural guidelines, and development standards.Requirements, design, and tasks: Structuring the development process around explicit specifications, including EARS requirements and Mermaid diagrams.Agent hooks: Automating recurring development activities, including security reviews, testing, code formatting, and documentation.Subagents: Delegating specialized tasks to multiple AI agents.Parallel task execution: Understanding task dependencies and coordinating concurrent execution.Kiro Workflows: Orchestrating multiple AI agents using sequential steps, parallel execution, and iterative loops.Cloud-based AI agents: Exploring continuously operating agents that support development, testing, monitoring, incident response, and other tasks.Best practices: Keep specifications synchronized with implementation, maintain detailed steering documents, and choose appropriate orchestration strategies.The presentation also discusses the importance of skills, powers, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers in extending the capabilities of AI-assisted development environments.A central theme is the changing role of software developers. As code generation becomes increasingly inexpensive, developers move toward higher levels of abstraction, focusing on goals, architecture, requirements, constraints, and quality standards.Rather than manually implementing every component, developers increasingly become orchestrators of AI agents, coordinating software creation through clear specifications and structured workflows.The key message is that the future of professional software development is not simply about generating more code faster. It is about building the right software while maintaining control, traceability, reliability, and alignment with human intent.These slides are intended for software developers, software architects, engineering managers, technical leaders, and anyone interested in understanding how AI agents and Spec-Driven Development are reshaping software engineering.Conference: All Day AI 2026Date: October 22, 2026Speaker: Haim MichaelConference website: https://www.alldayai.comSpeaker's post: https://lifemichael.com/en/sharing-my-experience-at-all-day-ai-2026/

items.title: Swift for ROS 2: iPhone, iPad and Mac in your ROS graph
items.summary: Talk at ROS By-The-Bay, October 22, 2026, hosted by Intrinsic.How an iPhone, an iPad or a Mac can join your ROS 2 graph as a real node, with no bridge.- Conduit: an App Store app that publishes 13 iPhone sensors (IMU, GPS, cameras, LiDAR, microphone, game controller, ARKit pose, ...) as standard ROS 2 messages over Zenoh or DDS, Humble to Rolling. Downloaded over 10,000 times.- swift-ros2 3.0: a native Swift client library in three packages that mirror upstream (rosidl, rclcpp, common_interfaces). Topics, services, actions and parameters with async/await, tested against Humble, Jazzy, Kilted and Lyrical hosts.- Conduit 3 sneak peek: Robots. Drive a mobile robot through its own camera, and teleoperate a MoveIt Servo arm from your phone.Conduit: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6757171237swift-ros2: https://github.com/swift-ros2Sneak peek videos: https://youtu.be/tERF16pEvUA / https://youtu.be/5x5xeL3mKAI
